records.themeTitle: Apparent help is not a substitute for discerning the right path
records.themeSummary: Trust belongs with genuine effort to subdue the inclination. Tzidkat HaTzadik adds that even apparent Divine assistance does not by itself prove that a person’s chosen course is right.
records.originHebrew: אַךְ שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלֶה עַל הַדַּעַת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַכֹּל הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, יוּכַל לֵילֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ לִבּוֹ בְּלֹא שׁוּם הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, וְיִסְמוֹךְ עַל עֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי", עַל זֶה מְסַיֵּים בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אִמְרַת ה' צְרוּפָה, מָגֵן הוּא לְכָל הַחֹסִים בּוֹ", וְהַיְינוּ לְמִי שֶׁמִּשְׁתַּדֵּל וּמִתְאַמֵּץ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ לִכְבוֹשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ בְּכָל כֹּחוֹ, וְחָפֵץ לַחֲסוֹת תַּחַת כְּנָפָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּמְצַפֶּה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּמִתְפַּלֵּל וּמִתְחַנֵּן לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, אָז מוּבְטָח שֶׁה' לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְּיָדוֹ, "מָגֵן הוּא לְכָל הַחֹסִים בּוֹ", שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁלוֹט בּוֹ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע כְּלָל, כְּעִנְיַן "מָגֵן" שֶׁמּוֹרֶה שֶׁמַּסְתִּיר אוֹתוֹ מִשּׂוֹנְאוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל לִקְרַב אֵלָיו כְּלָל.
records.originEnglish: But one must not think, God forbid, that because everything comes from the blessed God, one may follow the way of one’s heart without any effort and rely on the blessed God’s help, as in “For You are with me.” Against this, the Tanchuma concludes: “The utterance of the Lord is refined; He is a shield for all who take refuge in Him.” This refers to someone who exerts and strengthens himself, on his own side, to subdue his inclination with all his power; desires to take refuge beneath His blessed wings; looks to God; and prays and pleads before the Holy One, blessed be He. He is then assured that God will not leave him in the inclination’s hand. “He is a shield for all who take refuge in Him”: the evil inclination will have no power over him at all. A shield means that He conceals him from his enemy so that it cannot approach him at all.
records.targetHebrew: [סד] פְּעָמִים שֶׁרוֹאֶה בְּבֵירוּר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְסַיְּיעוֹ וּמַסְכִּים עִם מַעֲשָׂיו, עַל כָּל פָּנִים אֵינוֹ רְאָיָה כִּי מַעֲשָׂיו יְשָׁרִים בֶּאֱמֶת, וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "מַדְרִיכֲךָ בְּדֶרֶךְ תֵּלֵךְ" (יְשַׁעְיָה מח, יז), וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מַכּוֹת י:): בְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָדָם רוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ – מוֹלִיכִין אוֹתוֹ וְאָמַר "בְּדֶרֶךְ", דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בְּסֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי דֶּרֶךְ הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת מ"ח, כִּי אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְסַיֵּיעַ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי דַעְתּוֹ הוֹלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ הַתּוֹרָה; וּמַה שֶּׁלָּמְדוּ מִבִּלְעָם, גַּם לְפִי דַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל בִּלְעָם, כְּפִי סִטְרָא דִילֵיהּ, הָיָה דֶּרֶךְ זֶה יָשָׁר לוֹ כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא, וּמוּבָן. הֲלֹא תִרְאֶה בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין קיג.) שֶׁהָיָה קָשֶׁה לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲצִירַת הַגְּשָׁמִים, וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן אָמַר לוֹ לְאֵלִיָּהוּ: "לֵךְ... וְנִסְתַּרְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר", וְעֲזָרוֹ לְהִסָּתֵר מִפְּנֵי אַחְאָב בְּדֶרֶךְ נֵס, וְאִלּוּ סִיעַת אַחְאָב מוֹצְאוֹ הָיָה מַכְרִיחוֹ לְבַטֵּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אַחַר כָּךְ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה יְהוֹרָם לֶאֱלִישָׁע. וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא" (דְּבָרִים ל, יב), וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעֲזָרוּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּדֶרֶךְ נֵס לְהַרְאוֹת שֶׁהַדִּין עִמּוֹ, לֹא סָמְכוּ עַל זֶה (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא נט:), שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ שֶׁהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה. וְזֶה הָיְתָה גַּם כֵּן תְּלוּנַּת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: "אַתֶּם הֲמִתֶּם אֶת עַם ה'" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יז, ו), אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרָאוּ הַפְלָגַת הַנֵּס בְּאָבְדָם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם חָשְׁבוּ עַל זֶה כִּי "לֹא בַשָּׁמַיִם הִוא", וְאֵין לִסְמוֹךְ עַל זֶה שֶׁהַדִּין עִם מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נֶגֶד קֹרַח וַעֲדָתוֹ, רַק: אַתֶּם רְצִיתֶם לֵילֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה וּזְכוּתְכֶם גָּדוֹל, וּלְכָךְ הֲמִתֶּם וְגוֹמֵר:
records.targetEnglish: Sometimes a person clearly sees that the blessed God assists him and agrees with his actions. Nevertheless, this is not proof that his actions are truly upright. Of this it is said, “Who guides you on the way you go” (Isaiah 48:17), which our Sages interpret: “A person is led along the way he wishes to go” (Makkot 10b). It says “on the way”: in Proverbs this means the way of Torah, as I explained above in paragraph 48. For the blessed God assists only when, in the person’s own judgment, he is walking in the way of Torah. The proof learned from Balaam also follows Balaam’s own judgment, according to his side: this way was upright for him as he was; understand this. Consider Elijah: our Sages said (Sanhedrin 113a) that the withholding of rain was difficult before God. Nevertheless, He told Elijah, “Go … and hide,” and miraculously helped him conceal himself from Ahab. Had Ahab’s party found him, they would have compelled him to undo the decree, as happened afterward and as Jehoram did to Elisha. Of this it is said, “It is not in Heaven” (Deuteronomy 30:12): although God miraculously assisted Rabbi Eliezer in showing that the law agreed with him, the Sages did not rely upon that (Bava Metzia 59b). They considered that it was because he wished to go on that path. This was also Israel’s complaint, “You have caused the Lord’s people to die” (Numbers 17:6). Although they had seen the extraordinary miracle in the destruction of Korach’s company, they nevertheless reasoned that “it is not in Heaven”: one cannot rely on this to establish that the law agrees with Moses and Aaron against Korach and his company. Rather, you wished to go on this path, and your merit is great; therefore “you have caused,” and so forth.
records.explanation: Lech Lecha rejects following the heart’s desires while invoking “God is with me.” Tzidkat HaTzadik sharpens the test of that claim: an apparent sign of help, even a miracle, does not settle whether the chosen path is truly right. Its examples preserve the need for Torah’s judgment. This supports the active moral discernment demanded by Lech Lecha rather than contradicting its promise of help to those who truly seek refuge.
